hold_text: Tier-1 CI tooling whose diff touches two paths outside TIER1_SURFACE, so the guard cannot certify self-landing and a human merges. THE PATHS, named: (1) `scripts/check_strategy_coverage.py` — one of the 26 guard scripts that live in bare `scripts/` while their sibling `scripts/ci/**` is allowlisted, which is the exact case this hold_reason was added for in MI-226; (2) `config/regime_coverage_exemptions.yaml` — this guard's own exemption register, which `config/**` puts outside the allowlist even though it is guard data rather than runtime config. THAT SECOND CLAIM WAS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED: grepping the tree for readers of `regime_coverage_exemptions.yaml` returns exactly two, `scripts/check_strategy_coverage.py` and `scripts/research/regime_debt_matrix.py`, and ZERO under `src/` — with a positive control on the same probe, which finds five `src/` readers of `config/regime_policy.yaml`. The research reader takes only `coverage_debt` through a `.get()`, so the new top-level keys cannot disturb it. The remaining four paths (`docs/research/`, `docs/DOCUMENT-INDEX.md`, `docs/claude/performance-review-backlog.json`, `docs/strategy-coverage-matrix.md`) are all inside TIER1_SURFACE; the matrix is regenerated output, and the guard's own third registered step has `git_clean` on it, so it has to move in this PR. WHAT A HUMAN SHOULD READ, since that is the point of a hold: the two new invariants BOTH FAIL on `main` as it stands, and are therefore shipped armed against a single pinned waiver rather than hard. Arming them hard on 2026-09-12 would have turned every open PR in the repo red for a condition none of them caused. The waiver pins the measured pair (`observed_constant: 10`, `observed_min: 0`), re-fires if EITHER term moves, and FAILS if it is still present once the constant is fixed — so deleting it is cheaper than keeping it, which is the property this repo requires of an override. If that trade is judged wrong, the alternative is to land this together with the Tier-3 change to `src/runtime/intents.py` and drop the waiver, which is a different PR under a different tier. NO TIER-3 CHANGE IS TAKEN HERE. `src/runtime/intents.py` is READ ONLY in this diff. The constant and the five leg entries are PROPOSED in `docs/research/m20-u17-arbitration-fallback-inversion-2026-09-12.md` §3, including the one part the operator's 2026-09-09 answer does not settle — what value `slv_pullback_1d` gets, where its only rival is `execution: shadow` and the sibling-consistent 0 would create a tie that can hand SLV to a data-only leg.
